Senses.Explanation: Literally, "ten oxen." As a Chan title and label, it denotes Liangshan Kuoan's ordered set of ox-herding verses and the pictures made from them. A collection titles the work "Liangshan Kuoan Ze's Ten-Ox Verses" (梁山廓庵則和尚十牛頌); another record says, "our school has the account of herding the ox, and Liangshan has the verses on the Ten Oxen" (我宗門有牧牛之說，梁山有十牛之頌). The sequence begins with named sections including "seeking the ox" (尋牛) and "seeing the tracks" (見跡). The corpus also records direct criticism of its later handling: Baichi calls Liangshan's verses "compassionate, talk that descends into the weeds" (慈悲之故，落草之談), says later people "made a wrong move and then painted these Ten-Ox forms" (錯下手腳，更畫此十牛樣子), and urges burning them. In an encounter, a teacher interrupts a monk asked to recite the verses and asks, "Where is the ox?" (牛在甚麼處). The deviation from an ordinary count of cattle is documentary: "the Ten Oxen" (十牛) functions as the proper name of a Chan verse-and-picture series, circulated, recited, questioned, and criticized inside the record.
Senses.Note: Attested 33 times in 18 allowlisted texts. The title/series is primary and all curated occurrences concern that same work. Ordinary mentions of ten literal cattle, if encountered, would be a different thing, but the harvested allowlisted evidence did not establish such a second sense for this entry.

Senses.Explanation: A colloquial demonstrative: “thus,” “like this,” or “in this way.” It occurs 28,391 times in the allowlisted corpus and points to a stated situation without naming a new object. The Sixth Patriarch asks Huairang, “what thing comes thus?” (什麼物恁麼來); records also pair coming thus with going thus and say that thus, not-thus, and both together will not do. In public interviews it marks a student’s inference (恁麼則), a proposed understanding (恁麼會), the exact moment at issue (正當恁麼時), and a condition (若恁麼). A later citation doubles both sides: “thus, thus” and “not thus, not thus.” The variant spelling “thus” (與麼) is the same word. Chan makes this ordinary pointer a pervasive hinge of question and answer, but its deictic referent remains one sense.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide sense. Different grammatical frames and positive or negative appraisals are readings of the same demonstrative, not different things. The “if so, then” compound (恁麼則) has its own entry; link it without collapsing it into the base.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祖曰。什麼物恁麼來。曰說似一物即不中。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (景德傳燈錄), (南嶽懷讓) chapter. MasterName left null: two-speaker line. The Sixth Patriarch (祖 = 六祖 Huineng) asks the newly-arrived Huairang (什麼物恁麼來) 'what thing comes thus?'; Huairang answers (說似一物即不中). The (恁麼) is Huineng's, not the chapter-master Huairang's. The founding (恁麼) exchange.

Occurrences.Kwic: 頭曰。恁麼也不得。不恁麼也不得。恁麼不恁麼總不得。子作麼生。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (五燈會元), (藥山惟儼) chapter. (頭) = (石頭) (Shitou Xiqian) puts the double bind to Yaoshan: thus won't do, not-thus won't do, both-together won't do — then (子作麼生) ('you — what will you do?'). (恁麼) as the bare deictic driven to a triple negation.

Occurrences.Kwic: 又問。恁麼來不立。恁麼去不泯時如何。師曰。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (五燈會元), (洛浦元安) chapter. MasterName left null: two-speaker line. The coming/going pair (恁麼來) ('come thus') / (恁麼去) ('go thus') is spoken by an anonymous monk (又問…); Luopu Yuanan (師) only answers. The demonstrative is the monk's, not Luopu's.

Occurrences.Kwic: 賓云總不與麼。師便打。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (景德傳燈錄), (興化存獎) chapter. MasterName left null: two-speaker line. The (與麼) is spoken by the disciple Kebin (克賓, the precentor) — (賓云總不與麼) 'in no way thus' — and Xinghua strikes him (師便打, an action, not speech). The term is Kebin's, not Xinghua's. (Verbatim: 賓云總 ends lb 0295b10 and 不與麼 continues lb 0295b11, contiguous after tag-stripping.) Documents (與麼) as the graphic variant of (恁麼).

Occurrences.AttributionNote: A monk introduces an inference with “if so, then,” and the master reverses it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 纔恁麼會。蹉過了也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu appraises understanding it thus with the verdict that it has been missed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 且道。正當恁麼時如何。蟬聲時到耳。雁影忽迎眸。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A formal address uses “right at such a moment” and demands a response.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若恁麼見得。便有自由分。不隨一切語言轉。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu uses the demonstrative conditionally: “if seen thus.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 先德道恁麼恁麼又云不恁麼不恁麼
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A former worthy is cited doubling the positive form and then its negative counterpart.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: A monk proposes understanding it thus and asks what follows; the master answers.

Senses.Explanation: A conversational connective: 'being so' followed by 'then,' hence 'if so, then.' It occurs 5,426 times in 317 allowlisted texts. Chan encounter records give it a conspicuous turn-taking role: a questioner repeats or draws an inference from a master's answer, and the master may confirm, reverse, test, or reject that inference. Recorded replies call the inference wild talk, reverse its premise, block it with an image, ask for the student's own part, or demand how the claimed conclusion is carried out. These outcomes are deployments of the same connective, not new senses. Its distinctive role is the recurrent public-interview hinge where a proposed understanding becomes answerable to the next line.
Senses.Note: The high count reflects ordinary connective use across encounter dialogue. The phrase normally introduces the student's inference, but speaker role and the next response must be read from each exchange. Its demonstrative base, meaning 'being so,' and its following connective, meaning 'then,' remain one fixed compound here.

Occurrences.Kwic: 云恁麼則學人無著身處也。師曰。是爾著身處。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The student's inference that he has nowhere to lodge his body is immediately reversed by the master.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰恁麼則事同一家也。師曰。隔須彌在。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The student's same-household inference receives the contrary answer that Mount Sumeru separates them.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰恁麼則即相而無相也。師曰。也是狂言。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The master calls the student's inference wild talk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 云恁麼則音聲不入法界性也。師曰。離色求觀非正見。離聲求聽是邪聞。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The student's inference about sound is followed by a corrective answer about seeking seeing or hearing apart from their objects.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰。恁麼則順正歸元去也。師曰。歸元何順。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A student's inference about returning to the source is answered by challenging the claimed direction.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰：恁麼則絕於言句去也。師曰：夢裏惺惺。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The inference that the matter is cut off from words receives the reply 'awake within a dream.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧曰：恁麼則撒手那邊去也。師云：蝦跳不出斗。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The monk infers release on the far side; the master answers that a shrimp cannot jump out of the measure.

Occurrences.Kwic: 進云：「恁麼則均霑法利去也。」師云：「你本分事如何？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: After the student infers that all equally receive the benefit, the master asks about the student's own part.
